label: det-mismatch-diagnosis-2026-08-26
kind: read-only diagnosis of why 4 golden source schemes fail mark-total reconciliation
method: Parsed each PDF with DetParserSettings(escalate_on_mark_mismatch=False) so the question tree survives for inspection. ONLY the escalation was disabled. Nothing was written; no fixture, corpus file or committed scheme was touched.

HYPOTHESIS_FALSIFIED.hypothesis: #45's manifest floated that empty-cell defaulting interacts with lemely/io/det/rows.py flush(), which assigns stack[-1].marks only when q_row_had_answer is set -- so a leaf could carry answer_points whose marks never reach computed_total. Run 34 named this as the thing to check first.
HYPOTHESIS_FALSIFIED.test: For every leaf, compare q.marks against sum of its non-alternative answer_points' marks.
HYPOTHESIS_FALSIFIED.result: FALSIFIED for both deficit papers. 0625_s20_ms_31: 41 leaves, ZERO gap leaves. 0625_w21_ms_32: 43 leaves, ZERO gap leaves. Every leaf's q.marks exactly matches its answer points, so no marks are lost in propagation.
HYPOTHESIS_FALSIFIED.consequence: The deficits are NOT a marks-propagation defect. Recording the negative result explicitly so the next run does not re-test it.

0625_s20_ms_31.reading: Ids clean, distribution plausible for 0625 P3, leaves internally consistent. The 4 missing marks are CONTENT NOT CAPTURED, not marks mis-propagated. Where to look next: table selection (14 tables selected) and whether a question or part was skipped entirely.

0625_w21_ms_32.reading: Same shape as above. 7 marks of content not captured. 21 tables selected.

0606_s23_ms_12.OBSERVED_DEFECT_1: Top-level id '9' appears TWICE -- a duplicated top-level question.
0606_s23_ms_12.OBSERVED_DEFECT_2: Leaves worth 16 and 18 marks on an 80-mark Additional Mathematics paper. Stated as suspicion rather than proof: single questions of that tariff are implausible for 0606 P1, and the shape is CONSISTENT WITH total/summary rows being ingested as question leaves. 16+18=34 against a +36 overcount, which is suggestive but not a demonstration. WHAT WOULD CONFIRM IT: open those two leaves' text and check whether they are summary rows rather than questions.
0606_s23_ms_12.also: One leaf ('8c') carries q.marks=4 with zero answer points -- a mark minted from the marks column with no backing content.

0580_s23_ms_22.OBSERVED_DEFECT: The id sequence RESTARTS: '1', '2' and '8' each appear twice. Directly observed, not inferred.
0580_s23_ms_22.relation_to_45: #45 classified this paper as marks_cell_notation_not_parsed (3 empty cells defaulted, fully explaining the +3). That remains consistent -- but the duplicate top-level ids are a SEPARATE structural defect that #45's bucket does not describe, and it happens to net to the same +3.

what_this_changes_for_B4: The 'genuine_mark_total_mismatch' label on the two 0625 papers is now better characterised: leaves are internally consistent and ids are clean, so the deficit is un-captured content rather than a marks bug. That is a table-selection / question-extraction question.

Two papers show DUPLICATE TOP-LEVEL QUESTION IDS (0606 '9' twice; 0580 restarts at '1','2','8'). Duplicate ids are a structural parser defect independent of the mark totals, and would corrupt any leaf-keyed join even on papers that DO reconcile. Worth its own issue regardless of how B4 is decided.
Route 2 remains three different bugs. This diagnosis does not shrink it; it sharpens what each one is.
not_re_run: The #95 feasibility probe and #45's census were NOT re-run -- both are on disk at BUILD/accuracy-runs/golden-reparse-95-2026-08-26/ and BUILD/accuracy-runs/census-2026-08-24-b/.
